title: Utility-pole line is a blind sine route: a pole stands in the open Gauja, others in the parish road and at the old manor's door
evidence: Poles follow x = S.x+46+sin(z*0.004)*4 for z=-700..zEnd with no water/road/building checks. Pole 8 at (-140,-332) is 2.4m from the rendered river spline centreline — ~9m inside the 23.6m-wide water surface (both eras). Screenshot scratchpad/audit/y3-e4-pole-field-river.png shows the wire run crossing the Gauja on the water with the pole at the channel and the line then passing directly across the old manor house frontage — the pole at z=-194 computes to (-139.8,-194), ~5m from the manorHouse placed at (Mn.x-105, Mn.z-15)=(-145,-195) in eras 4/5. Poles 14 and 29-39 stand inside the hand-laid parish-road corridor (pole 14 is 0.85m from the road centreline). Data: xmod-out2.txt section 6.
fix_hint: Derive pole positions from the road polyline itself (walk roadsForEra points, offset perpendicular by ~8m) and skip any pole with distToRiver < 14; also clear the manor: skip() radius or distance test against MANOR.

title: Conifer crowns are sparse skeletons: needle cards float beside naked level-1 branches (anchors sit on level-2 twigs that have no tube geometry)
evidence: spruce/pine tubeMaxLevel:1 (src/treegen.js:786, 806) removes the level-2 twig tubes, but foliage anchorLevel is 2 with spacing 0.62/0.52 and pine tStart 0.3 (src/treegen.js:778, 798), so long bare level-1 branch tubes carry isolated floating needle combs. Screenshots: /tmp/.../audit/b3_pine_S.png (bare branch with one comb card near its tip, top-right shard slivers), b3_spruce_S.png / b3_spruce_SW.png (trunk visible through the crown, disconnected tufts).
fix_hint: Reduce foliage spacing (more anchors) and/or bump card sizeK for conifers so cards overlap the parent branch, or keep level-2 tubes with a stride like the broadleaf species (tubeStride 3).

title: Full-detail disc is ~2x sparser than the impostor ring around it — inverse LOD density seam at the 260 m boundary
evidence: Full tier is thinned by an extra `if (tier === 'full' && rng() < 0.5) continue;` (src/vegetation.js:391) that the far tier does not get. Probes in closed-forest zones, r=150m, era 1: KROGS full disc = 314 trees vs (200,-1500) far zone = 664 trees — the near/hero areas are half as dense as the backdrop, opposite of the 'near-closed canopy' intent (src/vegetation.js:384-386 comment, landuse.js:417-419). Visible as a denser far wall behind a parkland foreground in /tmp/.../audit/b3_brezga_pano.png and b3_boundary_out.png.
fix_hint: Drop or soften the 0.5 full-tier thin (e.g. 0.75 keep) — full caps are not saturated in era 1 (spruce 1393/2100, pine 989/1400) — or push the removed stems into the far list so density stays continuous across FULL_R.

title: Conifer foliage renders near-black at noon — spruces read as silhouettes against midday grass
evidence: Spruce/pine foliageColor 0.09-0.24 linear (src/treegen.js:785, 805) is further multiplied by crownAO strength 0.45 (src/treegen.js:648) and per-anchor age tint (1-a.age*0.25, src/treegen.js:603). At sky t=0.42 (noon) whole crowns render pitch black while grass and birches are bright: /tmp/.../audit/b3_spruce_SW.png, crop_edge_spruce.png, crop_T_spruce.png (giant black blocky crown shadows on the meadow).
fix_hint: Raise conifer card albedo ~1.5-2x or halve card crownAO strength; consider a small emissive/hemisphere lift on card backfaces so shaded needles stay dark green instead of black.

title: Far-tier instance caps silently truncate trees, and the row-major fill dumps the entire loss on the south of the map (Brežģa kalns belt)
evidence: Live in-page probe of the built artifact: oak far InstancedMesh is saturated — cap=42000 count=42000 (all other far meshes below cap, counts match the offline replica exactly, e.g. spruce 138,332). Replica: era-5 oak demand is 51,649 -> 9,649 oaks (19%) dropped, ALL at z 4152..6046 because fillTier/setEra clamps with Math.min(arr.length, capacity) (src/vegetation.js:528) and the placement grid fills rows z=-2640 -> z=+6040 — i.e. every dropped tree is around Brežģa kalns (z≈4969) and Brezgis/krogs (z≈5270), the family-hill area. Era 1 is much worse: spruce +47,717, pine +48,577, birch +41,126, oak +43,391 over cap (21-51% of each species dropped), all at z>~1834-4339 — the whole southern half of the 'primeval near-closed canopy' is thinned. CAPS at src/vegetation.js:221-225.
fix_hint: Size CAPS from measured per-era demand (era-1 far total is ~673k vs 566k capacity; era-5 oak needs ~52k), or make overflow spatially fair: when arr.length > cap, keep every k-th instance (stride = arr.length/cap) instead of truncating the tail, so the loss is diffuse rather than regional.

title: 2x stem-density step at the FULL_R=260 m ring: the forest is thinnest exactly where the player walks (the 6 POIs, incl. Brežģa kalns)
evidence: src/vegetation.js:388-391: tier = dp<260 ? 'full' : 'far'; then `if (tier === 'full' && rng() < 0.5) continue;` — inside 260 m of STEAD/MANOR/BREZGA/KROGS/CAMP/OAK the keep-probability is halved (falloff is already 1.0 there since 560/260>1), so stem density doubles abruptly when crossing the ring outward. Replica era 5: full-tier totals only 990 spruce + 745 pine + 547 birch + 154 oak across ALL six POI discs. Screenshot e5-brezga-south.png (cam 1650,292,4780 on Brežģa kalns looking south) shows the thin, trunk-gappy foreground against the denser far-impostor wall behind. Combined with finding 1 this makes the near-POI woods the sparsest in the sim — the places the walk mode actually visits.
fix_hint: Lower the full-tier rejection to ~0.25-0.3, or dither the tier transition (probabilistic full/far mix over 200-320 m) so no visible density ring; full caps (spruce 2100 etc.) have headroom — current era-5 usage is <50%.

title: Pond water edge hangs above the ground on its north and south-west rims
evidence: Pond disc (src/water.js:299-305, flat ellipse 52x34 at 186.3) vs basin carve (src/terrain.js:71-84) which only guarantees bed depth inside rr<0.7: measured rim heights are 185.30 at (-144,-290), 184.58 at (-144,-358), 184.88 at (-107,-348) — 1.0-1.7 m below the 186.3 surface, and the deeper river-channel carve passes under the ellipse. audit/e4-pond-N.png and crop-pond-edge.png show the pond plane terminating mid-air at its west edge with a tan wall face and shadow gap below the rim near the dam.
fix_hint: Widen the dished-bed stamp so the ellipse edge (rr=1) lands on ground raised to >= POND_LEVEL+0.2 (add an outer berm ring to the basin carve), or shrink the pond ellipse to the carved basin.

title: Bright cyan 'aquarium glass' stripe along shores: the ribbon's EDGE_DROP rim wall is exposed wherever banks are sunken
evidence: src/water.js:61-98 ribbon profile drops the outer verts by EDGE_DROP (0.5 for the Gauja, :149) as a near-vertical rim meant to be hidden inside the bank; because the bank ground is carved below the waterline (finding 1), this rim face is visible from walking level as a continuous bright cyan band under the dark water along whole reaches. Visible at all three river spots in both eras: crop-A-edge.png (broad cyan stripe between sand wall and water), e1-A-east.png, e1-B-east.png, e1-C-east.png.
fix_hint: Fixing the bank carve/skirt drape (finding 1) hides the rim; additionally tint the two outer UV bands of the ribbon darker (they already have distinct u=0/0.04 coords) so any residual exposed rim doesn't read as glowing glass.
